body.statement:
Fix \(r\), \(K\), and an incoherence envelope \(\mu>1\).  Positive constants \(c_0,c_1,c_2\), depending only on these fixed quantities, \(q\), and the aspect bounds, exist such that, for all sufficiently large \(n,m\), whenever \(b_{nm}\le c_0\) and \(\lambda_{nm}\le c_1B\sqrt{nm}\),
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)}
 E_P[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U)]\ge c_2b_{nm}.
\]
The bound already holds on an independent constant-propensity submodel with \(p_{ij}=q\), so observing \(p\) does not weaken it.  The strict slack \(\mu>1\) is needed by the continuous local row packing used here.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(t=m/n\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:aspect\mbox{-}ratio}\) gives \(t\in[c_-,c_+]\).  Choose \(c_0<1\).  On the regime \(b_{nm}\le c_0\), the truncation in \(\mathrm{def:frontier\mbox{-}rate}\) is inactive, and hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 b_{nm}
 &=\frac{B}{\lambda_{nm}}K r^{3/2}\mu q^{-1/2}
   \sqrt{\log(en)}\sqrt{nm}\sqrt{n^{-1}+nm^{-2}}\\
 &=K r^{3/2}\mu\sqrt{t+t^{-1}}
   \frac{B}{\lambda_{nm}}\sqrt{\frac{n\log(en)}q}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus, with
\[
 s_{nm}:=\frac{B}{\lambda_{nm}}\sqrt{\frac{n\log(en)}q},
\]
there are positive constants \(C_-\) and \(C_+\), depending only on \(r,K,\mu,c_-,c_+\), such that
\[
 C_-s_{nm}\le b_{nm}\le C_+s_{nm}.
 \tag{1}
\]

We construct a constant-propensity subexperiment.  Since \(r\) is fixed, partition \(I\) into disjoint balanced blocks \(I_1,\ldots,I_r\), and partition \(J\) into disjoint balanced blocks \(J_1,\ldots,J_r\); within each partition, block sizes differ by at most one.  Write \(N_s=|I_s|\) and \(M_s=|J_s|\).  For \(s\ge2\), let \(u_s=N_s^{-1/2}{\bf 1}_{I_s}\), viewed in \(\mathbb R^n\), and, for every \(s\), let \(v_s=M_s^{-1/2}{\bf 1}_{J_s}\), viewed in \(\mathbb R^m\).  Let \(u_0=N_1^{-1/2}{\bf 1}_{I_1}\).  Fix \(k_0\in I_1\).  For every \(k\in\mathcal K:=I_1\setminus\{k_0\}\), define
\[
 w_k=\frac{e_k-e_{k_0}}{\sqrt2},\qquad
 \delta=a\frac{B}{\lambda_{nm}}\sqrt{\frac{\log(en)}q},\qquad
 u_k=\frac{u_0+\delta w_k}{\sqrt{1+\delta^2}},
 \tag{2}
\]
where the fixed constant \(a>0\) will be chosen below.  The vectors \(u_0\) and \(w_k\) are orthogonal unit vectors, so \(u_k\) is a unit vector.  Disjoint block supports give
\[
 U_k=(u_k,u_2,\ldots,u_r)\in\mathbb O_{n,r},
 \qquad V=(v_1,\ldots,v_r)\in\mathbb O_{m,r}.
\]
Also set \(U_0=(u_0,u_2,\ldots,u_r)\), and define
\[
 M_k=\lambda_{nm}U_kV^\top\quad(k\in\mathcal K),
 \qquad M_0=\lambda_{nm}U_0V^\top.
 \tag{3}
\]

We verify every model restriction.  From (1)--(2),
\[
 \delta\sqrt n=a s_{nm}\le aC_-^{-1}b_{nm}\le aC_-^{-1}c_0.
 \tag{4}
\]
For a row in \(I_1\), the triangle inequality and (2) give
\[
 \lVert e_i^\top U_k\rVert_2
 \le N_1^{-1/2}+\delta/\sqrt2.
 \tag{5}
\]
For a row in \(I_s\), \(s\ge2\), its row norm is \(N_s^{-1/2}\).  Since \(r\) is fixed and the blocks are balanced,
\[
 \max_s\sqrt{n/N_s}\longrightarrow\sqrt r.
\]
The strict inequality \(\mu>1\) supplies positive slack between \(\sqrt r\) and \(\sqrt{\mu r}\).  First choose \(ac_0\) small enough, depending only on that slack and the fixed constants in (4), and then take \(n\) sufficiently large.  Equations (4)--(5) yield
\[
 \lVert U_k\rVert_{2,\infty}\le\sqrt{\mu r/n}.
 \tag{6}
\]
The same balanced-block calculation, without the perturbation, gives
\[
 \lVert V\rVert_{2,\infty}\le\sqrt{\mu r/m}
 \tag{7}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(m\).  Thus (6)--(7) verify the two incoherence assumptions.  By (3), all \(r\) nonzero singular values of \(M_k\) equal \(\lambda_{nm}\).  Consequently exact rank, the signal floor, and the condition-number bound hold, the last because \(1\le K\).

For all sufficiently large dimensions, balanced blocks satisfy \(N_s\ge n/(2r)\) and \(M_s\ge m/(2r)\).  Equations (2)--(3) imply
\[
 \max_{i,j}|(M_k)_{ij}|
 \le \frac{2r\lambda_{nm}}{\sqrt{nm}}
     +aB\sqrt{\frac{2r\log(en)}{qm}}.
 \tag{8}
\]
Choose \(c_1>0\) so that \(2rc_1\le1/4\).  Under \(\lambda_{nm}\le c_1B\sqrt{nm}\), the first term in (8) is at most \(B/4\).  The second is at most \(B/4\) for all sufficiently large \(n,m\), because \(q,r,a\) are fixed and aspect ratio is bounded.  Hence
\[
 \max_{i,j}|(M_k)_{ij}|\le B/2
 \tag{9}
\]
uniformly over \(k\in\mathcal K\cup\{0\}\).

For each \(k\in\mathcal K\cup\{0\}\), define a law \(P_k\) by setting \(Y_{ij}(0)=0\).  Independently over cells, draw \(Y_{ij}(1)\in\{-B,B\}\) with
\[
 P_k\{Y_{ij}(1)=B\}
 =h_{k,ij}:=\frac12\left(1+\frac{(M_k)_{ij}}B\right).
 \tag{10}
\]
Independently of all potential outcomes and independently over cells, draw \(A_{ij}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q)\), and record \(p_{ij}=q\).  Equation (9) puts every \(h_{k,ij}\) in \([1/4,3/4]\), while (10) gives \(E_{P_k}[Y_{ij}(1)]=(M_k)_{ij}\).  Independence from all preceding cells in the row-major filtration gives
\[
 \mu^1_{ij}=E_{P_k}[Y_{ij}(1)\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]=(M_k)_{ij},
 \qquad \mu^0_{ij}=0.
 \tag{11}
\]
Thus the causal effect matrix \(M=\mu^1-\mu^0\) is exactly \(M_k\), rather than being defined from the observed score.  Independence of \(A_{ij}\) from the potential outcomes after conditioning on the recorded past verifies sequential randomization.  The equality \(p_{ij}=q<1/2\) verifies overlap, and the support in (10), together with \(Y_{ij}(0)=0\), verifies bounded outcomes.  Equations (6)--(7), the singular-value calculation, and the aspect assumption verify all remaining member properties.  Hence
\[
 P_k\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)
 \quad\text{for every }k\in\mathcal K\cup\{0\}.
 \tag{12}
\]

We bound the information in \(\mathcal O_{n,m}=\sigma(A,Y,p)\).  If \(x,y\in[-B/2,B/2]\), put \(s=(1+x/B)/2\) and \(t'=(1+y/B)/2\).  For fixed \(t'\in[1/4,3/4]\), the Bernoulli relative entropy
\(f(s)=s\log(s/t')+(1-s)\log((1-s)/(1-t'))\) satisfies
\[
 f(t')=f'(t')=0,
 \qquad f''(s)=\frac1{s(1-s)}\le\frac{16}3
 \quad\text{on }[1/4,3/4].
\]
Taylor's theorem therefore gives
\[
 \operatorname{kl}\left(\frac{1+x/B}{2},\frac{1+y/B}{2}\right)
 \le \frac{2}{3}\frac{(x-y)^2}{B^2}.
 \tag{13}
\]
The assignment law and recorded propensity are identical under \(P_k\) and \(P_0\).  Conditional on \(A_{ij}=0\), the observed outcome is the common value zero; conditional on \(A_{ij}=1\), it has Bernoulli sign parameter \(h_{k,ij}\).  Independence over cells, (13), and direct factorization of the product likelihood yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(P_k^{\mathcal O},P_0^{\mathcal O})
 &=q\sum_{i,j}\operatorname{kl}(h_{k,ij},h_{0,ij})\\
 &\le \frac{Cq}{B^2}\lVert M_k-M_0\rVert_F^2.
\end{aligned}
 \tag{14}
\]
Only the first singular component differs in (3), and \(\lVert v_1\rVert_2=1\), so
\[
 \lVert M_k-M_0\rVert_F^2
 =\lambda_{nm}^2\lVert u_k-u_0\rVert_2^2.
\]
Orthogonality in (2) gives
\[
 \lVert u_k-u_0\rVert_2^2
 =2\left(1-\frac1{\sqrt{1+\delta^2}}\right)
 \le\delta^2.
\]
Substitution of (2) into (14) proves
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_k^{\mathcal O},P_0^{\mathcal O})
 \le Ca^2\log(en).
 \tag{15}
\]

The alternatives are separated in the required rowwise loss.  If \(k,\ell\in\mathcal K\) are distinct, inspect row \(k\).  On that row only the first columns of \(U_k\) and \(U_\ell\) can be nonzero, and (2) gives
\[
 \lVert e_k^\top U_k\rVert_2-\lVert e_k^\top U_\ell\rVert_2
 =\frac{\delta}{\sqrt{2(1+\delta^2)}}.
\]
Right multiplication by any \(R\in\mathbb O_r\) preserves row norms.  The reverse triangle inequality therefore gives
\[
 \min_{R\in\mathbb O_r}\lVert U_kR-U_\ell\rVert_{2,\infty}
 \ge\frac{\delta}{\sqrt{2(1+\delta^2)}}.
\]
Thus
\[
 \mathcal L(U_k,U_\ell)
 \ge \Delta_{nm}:=\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
       \frac{\delta}{\sqrt{2(1+\delta^2)}}.
 \tag{16}
\]
Equation (4) implies \(\delta\to0\), so eventually \(\delta\le1\).  Combining (1), (2), and (16), and using \(t\in[c_-,c_+]\), gives a constant \(c>0\) such that
\[
 \Delta_{nm}\ge c b_{nm}.
 \tag{17}
\]
Indeed, before the bounded denominator factor in (16), the exact ratio is
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{n/(\mu r)}\,\delta}{b_{nm}}
 =\frac{a}{K r^2\mu^{3/2}\sqrt{t+t^{-1}}}.
\]

It remains to derive the multiple-testing reduction.  Let \(D=|\mathcal K|=N_1-1\), let \(\Theta\) be uniform on \(\mathcal K\), and conditionally on \(\Theta=k\) draw the observed experiment from \(P_k^{\mathcal O}\).  With \(\overline P=D^{-1}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}P_k^{\mathcal O}\), expansion of the logarithms gives
\[
 I(\Theta;\mathcal O)
 =\frac1D\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\operatorname{KL}(P_k^{\mathcal O},\overline P)
 =\frac1D\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\operatorname{KL}(P_k^{\mathcal O},P_0^{\mathcal O})
  -\operatorname{KL}(\overline P,P_0^{\mathcal O}).
\]
Nonnegativity of relative entropy and (15) imply
\[
 I(\Theta;\mathcal O)\le Ca^2\log(en).
 \tag{18}
\]
For any decoder \(\widehat\Theta\), let \(P_e=P(\widehat\Theta\ne\Theta)\).  Conditioning the entropy of \(\Theta\) first on the error indicator yields
\[
 H(\Theta\mid\mathcal O)\le\log2+P_e\log D.
\]
Since \(H(\Theta)=\log D\), this and (18) give
\[
 P_e\ge1-\frac{Ca^2\log(en)+\log2}{\log D}.
 \tag{19}
\]
Balanced blocks give \(D\asymp n\).  Choose \(a>0\) sufficiently small, depending only on the fixed quantities, so the right side of (19) is at least \(1/2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).

Finally take any \(\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}\) and decode by a nearest member of \(\{U_k:k\in\mathcal K\}\) in the orthogonal-quotient \(2,\infty\) distance.  This quotient distance obeys the triangle inequality: compose two orthogonal alignments and use invariance of row norms under right orthogonal multiplication.  Thus, on a decoding error under \(P_k\), pairwise separation (16) and nearest-neighbor decoding imply
\[
 \mathcal L(\widetilde U,U_k)\ge\Delta_{nm}/2.
\]
Averaging over the uniform index, using (19), and then (17), gives
\[
 \sup_{k\in\mathcal K}E_{P_k}[\mathcal L(\widetilde U,U_k)]
 \ge\frac{\Delta_{nm}}4
 \ge c_2b_{nm}.
\]
By (12), this finite family is a subset of the frozen predictable class, and it has \(p_{ij}=q\) at every cell.  Taking the supremum over the full class and then the infimum over \(\widetilde U\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}\) proves the theorem.
body.justification: The converse supplies the information-theoretic lower endpoint in the common expected normalized maximum-row risk.
body.gap: It proves order \(b_{nm}\) only as a lower benchmark; it does not match the constant hybrid upper endpoint.
body.consumer: Trial designers obtain a lower benchmark linking decision budget, outcome scale, and signal strength.
